sources.citation: OLAC: Resources in and about the Busami language [bsm] (Internet Archive copy 2026-06-15).
sources.note: Catalogue record only: lists just transnewguinea.org, Glottolog and Ethnologue for bsm -- no SIL, PARADISEC or other archival descriptions exist.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David C. 2014. Austronesians in Papua: Diversification and change in South Halmahera-West New Guinea. PhD dissertation, UC Berkeley.
sources.note: Busami data are second-hand (Silzer 1983). Sec. 5.4 reconstructs penultimate stress for Proto-SHWNG from descriptions of Buli, Sawai, Taba, Ambai, Wandamen, Waropen, Warembori; Busami is not among the languages with any stress description. p. 38 reports Price & Donohue (2008 ms) claim that 'other languages of Yapen also have complex stress systems' without Busami specifics.

sources.citation: Silzer, Peter J. 1983. Ambai: an Austronesian language of Irian Jaya, Indonesia. PhD thesis, Australian National University.
sources.note: No Busami phonology. Busami appears in the lexicostatistic table and in Appendix A pp. 237-238, where Silzer says the two Ambai verb-stem stress classes 'are also present in the other [Yapen] languages. All Yapen languages, except Busami, exhibit different patterns of interaction between the infixes /-u-/ and /-i-/ with verbs with the initial syllable of the stem stressed and those with the initial syllable of the verb unstressed' -- an oblique remark, not a statement of where Busami word stress falls.

sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon J. (ed.). transnewguinea.org: 'Busami' (lexicon of 6 items from Voorhoeve 1975).
sources.note: Wordlist only, no stress marks.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid busa1254 'Busami' (record, page, reference list).
sources.note: Bibliographic record only: 2 references (Anceaux 1961 = Glottolog's most extensive description, 'wordlist or less'; Ethnologue 28). No grammar, sketch or phonology listed.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa (Kemendikdasmen). Peta Bahasa: 'Bahasa Busami', Provinsi Papua (entry idb=347). Jakarta: Badan Bahasa. Online database entry, accessed 2026-09-20.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content: location, neighbouring villages, other languages spoken in Kamanaf (Ansus, Onate), and a dialectometric statement ('isolek Busami merupakan sebuah bahasa dengan persentase perbedaan berkisar 81%-100%' vs Munggui, Maraw, Poom, Onate, Ansus). Implies Badan Bahasa collected a Busami wordlist (unpublished).

sources.citation: Gasser, Emily & Montreal Benesch. 2025. An un-Austronesian Austronesian language: Proto-Western Yapen and its lexicon. NUSA: Linguistic studies of languages in and around Indonesia 77-78: 39-60.
sources.note: nothing: the words stress/accent/tone do not occur in the article; Busami is only listed.

sources.citation: Gasser, Emily. 2017. Papuan-Austronesian language contact on Yapen Island: a preliminary account. NUSA 62: 101-155.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Busami information only from Anceaux 1961 (p. 114: Anceaux 'does not give actual forms'); confirms no independent Busami data were available to the author.

sources.citation: Gasser, Emily. 2015. The development of verbal infixation in Cenderawasih Bay. In Malcolm Ross & I Wayan Arka (eds.), Language change in Austronesian languages: Papers from 12-ICAL, volume 3 (Asia-Pacific Linguistics 018 / Studies on Austronesian Languages 004), 1-17. Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics, ANU.
sources.note: Busami appears only in table (2) of singular agreement affixes (Busami: 1sg yau ya-, 2sg au w-/-u-, 3sg i s-/-i-) and in the remark that the 1sg prefix 'surfaces as [ya-] in at least some environments in Busami and Biak'. On stress the chapter says only (fn. 11, p. 9): 'It is plausible that PBY had largely penultimate stress and disyllabic roots, but this has not been definitively shown.. Stress throughout Austronesian is predominantly penultimate (Klamer 2002a; Blust 2009), but information on stress in the languages of West Papua is scarce. In Wamesa, stress on verb roots is largely penultim…

sources.citation: Price, David S. & Mark Donohue. 2009. Report on the Ansus survey, West Yapen Island, Papua, Indonesia. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009-001.
sources.note: Busami only in language lists and lexicostatistic remarks ('Busami is not closely related to any other language in the area'; 600 speakers). Phonological appendix concerns Ansus only. Nothing on Busami stress.

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene S.L. (comp.). 1998-. Numeral Systems of the World's Languages: 'Busami' (Yapen, Papua, Indonesia). Data provided by Heljä Clouse, SIL Irian Jaya, 11 January 1993, taken from an SIL linguistic survey list (1992). Leipzig: MPI-EVA (lingweb).
sources.note: no phonology content: numerals 1 bo-siri, 2 bo-ru, 3 bo-toru, 4 bo-ati, 5 ri/riŋ, 6 wonaŋ, 7 ruwu-varu, 8 toro-varu, 9 aro-varu, 10 sura, 20 piarei, without stress marks; comment on the five/twenty counting system and endangerment only.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 1991. Sound change and migration distance. In Robert Blust (ed.), Currents in Pacific linguistics: Papers on Austronesian languages and ethnolinguistics in honour of George W. Grace (Pacific Linguistics C-117), 27-42. Canberra: Research School of Pacific Studies, Australian National University. (ANU Open Research hdl 1885/253742; text)
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone for any language (the words do not occur in the paper). Busami's only appearance is p. 35: 'EV = 3.0: (Wandamen, Waropen, Ansus, Woi, Pom, Marau, Munggui, Papuma, Busami, Serui-Laut, Ambai, Wadapi-Laut, Kurudu, Sera, Sissano, Tumleo)', i.e. PAN *p is lost (erosion value 3.0) in Busami -- a single second-hand segmental datum, no phonological description.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1978. A little Mor. In S.A. Wurm & Lois Carrington (eds.), Second International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics: Proceedings, fascicle 1: Western Austronesian (Pacific Linguistics C-61), 285-316. Canberra: Research School of Pacific Studies, Australian National University. (ANU Open Research hdl 1885/253213; text)
sources.note: Nothing about Busami prosody. The paper's stress/tone remarks (sec. 4 Phonology, pp. 290-291: phoneme inventory '+ stress + tone'; 'Stress is unpredictable, and is written in the lexicon when there is a clear stressed syllable; but it is more likely that stress is a feature of the tonal system, which has not been fully analysed. Tonal minimal pairs abound..') concern Mor only. Busami appears twice: Table I p. 286 (lexicostatistic percentage with Mor, 34%/110, from Anceaux 1961) and Appendix B p. 305 (item 128c 'STONE': 'Busami worami'), i.e. one unaccented second-hand lexical form.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C.L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Entry 181 Busami (Ac): a ~10-item wordlist (anduta, wesen, bo-siri, una, renso, ena, worami, boru, maria), no stress marks, no phonology.

sources.citation: Anceaux, J.C. 1961. The linguistic situation in the islands of Yapen, Kurudu, Nau and Miosnum, New Guinea. Verhandelingen KITLV 35. 's-Gravenhage: Martinus Nijhoff. 166 pp. (OAPEN open access, DOI 10.26530/oapen_613371)
sources.note: Nothing on Busami stress. Busami = section J, printed p. 8 (p. 16): 'It is to be regretted that only scant information could be collected about this language'. Transcription note printed p. 14 (p. 22): 'Stress-accent, vowel pitch and vowel length (part of the accentual system in many of these languages) are not indicated.' The book's only accent remark concerns Papuma (p. 7). Busami forms appear unaccented throughout the comparative word-list and correspondence sets.
